messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 PAGE: multiple customers reporting 502s / TLS handshake failures to hosted-api-east. Paging oncall. Impact: user-facing inference requests failing. See outage tag: #outage-tls-east

Nora (oncall): I'm on it. Can folks drop quick checks here — are other regions affected?

Maya (Customer Success): Getting inbound from two enterprise customers in EU — they see errors originating from hosted-east. They reported spikes starting ~ 06:35 UTC.

Ryan (oncall): I'm taking lead. Assigning tasks: Andy — SRE triage & logs. Sam — network checks (VPC peering + MTU). Lei — look for inference-level anomalies. Nora — coordinate customer comms.

Andy (eng-sre): Confirmed TLS handshake failures in load-balancer logs: lots of `alert handshake failure` and `SSL3_GET_CLIENT_HELLO:error` entries. Tail from lb-03: 
```
Apr 07 06:36:12 lb-03 ssl: [error] SSL alert number 40: handshake failure client_ip=10.22.33.44:54212
Apr 07 06:36:12 lb-03 ssl: [warn] client hello parse fail: truncated cert chain?
```
Also seeing increased 502s proxied to backend pool.

Sam (netops): From the network side: VPC peering is healthy per control plane. I ran a quick mtu check between subnets, and noticed some hosts in the east-az1 path returning 1400 MTU instead of expected 9000. Could be PMTU/fragmentation related. Capturing pcap from host-gw-1 now.

Lei (eng-ml): Model servers are up; KV cache hits normal. No CPU or memory spikes. However, a subset of TLS handshakes against our TLS termination stack fails early — the backend sees zero bytes after ClientHello in those sessions.

Andy (eng-sre): Adding timeline notes:
- 06:33 UTC: automated cert-rotation job kicked for hosted-east (staged rollout).
- 06:35 UTC: first increase in TLS alerts in LB logs.
- 06:36 UTC: customer pages start.
Hypothesis A: Incomplete cert chain deployed on LB during rotation -> some clients reject and handshake abort.
Hypothesis B: MTU/fragmentation causing ClientHello (or SNI extension) fragmentation and TLS stack fails to reassemble -> handshake error.

Sam (netops): PCAP from host-gw-1 shows `ICMP Fragmentation Needed` occasional messages and lots of 1514B frames. Example tcpdump snippet: 
```
06:35:58.123456 IP 10.0.1.45.54212 > 10.0.2.11.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1411, ack 1, win 65535, length 1410
06:35:58.123789 IP 10.0.2.11 > 10.0.1.45: ICMP 3/4 Frag needed and DF set, mtu 1400
```
That supports PMTU issues.

Nora (oncall): OK — dual track: 1) immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact, 2) RCA work in-thread. Mitigations: divert traffic from hosted-east LB to hosted-west for critical customers; temporarily pin to dedicated nodes that bypass the rotated certs. Ryan — can you trigger region failover for top-10 customers?

Ryan (oncall): Doing it now. Will update route table for customer-overlay to prefer west. Deploy-bot: initiate canary reroute for 10% traffic first.

deploy-bot: Canary reroute initiated: customers [alpha-suite] -> hosted-west (10%). Monitor for errors.

Maya (Customer Success): Messaging customers: sending short update to affected enterprise customers — letting them know we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA.

Andy (eng-sre): More logs from the cert-rotation job: rotation job completed on lb-01 and lb-02; lb-03 returned non-zero exit for intermediate chain concat step. Job log: 
```
[2026-04-07T06:33:05Z] cert-rotator: fetched new leaf and intermediate PEMs
[2026-04-07T06:33:12Z] cert-rotator: concatenated chain -> /etc/ssl/certs/chain.pem
[2026-04-07T06:33:12Z] cert-rotator: reload nginx -> exit 1 (short read)
[2026-04-07T06:33:13Z] cert-rotator: exit with code 1, leaving partial chain on disk
```
So lb-03 has a partially written chain file. That maps to Hypothesis A.

Sam (netops): But PCAP evidence shows ICMP frag messages concurrent with the first failed handshakes. Could be both issues amplifying: partial chain -> some clients try again with larger ClientHello (extension sizes), then fragmentation triggers parse errors.

Lei (eng-ml): If clients send large SNI/ALPN extension sets (some mobile SDKs include many ALPN tokens), fragmentation could split ClientHello and older TLS stacks might reject. Can we reproduce locally by forcing DF on path with reduced MTU?

Andy (eng-sre): Repro attempt: on a test VM, set mtu to 1400 and run `openssl s_client -connect lb-03:443 -servername hosted-east`. Result: sometimes handshake fails with `ssl: error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number` — intermittent. When I replace chain.pem with full proper chain, failure rate drops but not to zero under low MTU. Repro indicates both issues matter.

Nora (oncall): Immediate actions checklist (in-thread):
- [x] Reroute top customers to hosted-west canary (Ryan)
- [x] Rotate lb-03 to previous cert snapshot (Andy) -> temporary rollback executed at 06:47 UTC
- [x] Netops: enforce consistent MTU on east-az1 path (Sam) -> pushing config to gw nodes now
- [x] CS notify customers (Maya)
- [ ] Post-mortem and RCA once stable (owners: Andy + Sam)

Sam (netops): Config pushed to gateways to clamp to 9000 -> verifying. Also found a single peering appliance that had defaulted to 1500 MTU during an unrelated maintenance window; correcting and flushing routes now.

Andy (eng-sre): After rollback of lb-03 chain and MTU fix, handshake error rate dropped from 12% -> 0.7% over 10 minutes. Backend 502s falling. Telemetry:
```
06:46 -> 06:56 error-rate went 12% -> 0.7%
06:48 customer pages start resolving
06:50 most canaries healthy
```
We should keep the mitigation for 30m before full rollback.

Lei (eng-ml): Adding hypothesis tracking for postmortem: 
- Hypothesis A (primary): cert-rotator partial write on lb-03 produced truncated chain -> TLS stacks reject or behave unexpectedly. Evidence: failed concat exit code + partial file.
- Hypothesis B (secondary): MTU mismatch/fragmentation caused ClientHello fragmentation and handshake parsing errors. Evidence: ICMP Frag needed messages and tcpdump.
- Hypothesis C (amplifier): certain clients with long SNI/ALPN ext triggered larger ClientHellos, exposing fragmentation + partial chain together. Evidence: more errors from SDK-heavy mobile clients.

Maya (Customer Success): Customers updated. One flagged they had retries built-in and saw transient errors but no data loss. Good to note in RCA.

Andy (eng-sre): Action items for RCA: 
- Andy: root cause confirm and clean up cert-rotator idempotency + atomic write 
- Sam: audit MTU config across all peering appliances + add PMTU monitoring alert 
- Lei: produce test harness to fuzz ClientHello sizes across MTU boundaries and run against our LB TLS stack 
- Nora: draft summary for execs once postmortem ready

Ryan (oncall): Closing incident timeline: mitigation in place and customer impact minimized. I'll leave the channel open for RCA notes.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-2026-045 closed to P1->P2. Final status: degraded for ~14 minutes; mitigation applied (rollback + network fix).

Nora (oncall): Thanks everyone. Will coordinate postmortem doc and assign owners per action items. If you have log snippets, drop them here before we rotate to the PM.

Andy (eng-sre): Dropping the cert-rotator stack trace here for PM: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/opt/cert-rotator/rotator.py", line 214, in write_chain
    with open('/etc/ssl/certs/chain.pem','w') as f:
OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device
```
That explains why concat failed on lb-03 — ephemeral disk full during atomic rename. We'll add pre-checks.

Sam (netops): Also adding the traceroute output that shows the peering hop that had MTU 1500 set incorrectly.
```
traceroute to 10.0.2.11 (10.0.2.11), 30 hops max
 1  gw-01 (10.0.0.1)  0.2 ms
 2  peer-node (10.100.5.1)  2.3 ms  (MTU 1500)
 3  10.0.2.11  3.1 ms
```

Lei (eng-ml): I'll build the fuzz harness and run against a local instance of our TLS stack; will post results and test vectors in the PM doc.

Maya (Customer Success): I'll follow up with customers with final update once RCA doc ready.

Nora (oncall): Great work. Summary for the channel: transient P1 caused by combination of cert-rotator partial write (disk full) on lb-03 + MTU mismatch on one peering hop -> caused TLS handshake failures. Mitigations: rollback chain on lb-03, enforce correct MTU, reroute critical customers. Postmortem owners assigned. Closing thread when PM draft posted. :white_check_mark:
